_comment: Allowed-deviation gate for the marketing suite (python3 scripts/visual_parity.py --suite marketing).
Every entry is a GATE, not a comment: it carries a measurable bound, vp_compare re-measures it from each run's capture, and it goes FAIL if the page stops meeting it.
Metrics: doc_height (min px), text_present / text_absent (a regex over every rendered text node).
Only deviations the build ALREADY satisfies are listed. Differences that are still open are findings in findings/*.json, not entries here:
an entry for a defect would be red from day one, and a gate that starts red authorises being ignored.

deviations.retire_when: never while the legal pages render the generated drafts; if Figma is redrawn around the real documents, re-measure the bound
deviations.source: ClickUp 17tnw2b0x3g (PR #142, e7566a96): the drafts in docs/legal/ are generated into src/lib/legal/*.generated.ts and rendered by src/components/legal/LegalPage.vue
deviations.reason: Figma designs the page chrome around placeholder prose. The build carries the full draft, so it is several times taller. The gate fails if the page falls back to placeholder length, which would mean the real text was removed.

deviations.retire_when: the downloads backend returns real artefacts (ClickUp 86ak10afm) and the buttons are wired; then replace this entry with a check for the real label

deviations.source: DEC-007 rejected OIDC; the API has no social login (audit finding signin-03, class C, owner decision pending)
